title: Past Perfect Continuous
tagline: how long something had been happening
why: This tense explains a past situation: how long something had been going on, or why someone looked tired, wet or upset. It makes your stories clearer and more natural.
understand: Her eyes were red because she had been crying.
able: say how long something had been happening before another past moment
give the reason for a past situation you could see or feel
ask How long had you been ... ? correctly
mistakes: I had been knowing him for years.
When I met her, she was living in Toronto for five years.
When I met her, she had been living in Toronto for five years.
She was tired because she has been working all day.
She was tired because she had been working all day.
I had been write emails all morning.
I had been writing emails all morning.
How long you had been living there?
How long had you been living there?
use: how long an activity went on before a past moment: I had been driving for six hours when I stopped.
the reason for a past result: The grass was wet because it had been raining.
with for and since in a past story: They had been dating since 2019 when they got engaged.
form: I / she / they had been working. Short form: I'd been working.
He hadn't been sleeping well. We had not been listening.
Had you been waiting long? How long had she been living there?
signals: for two hours, since Monday, all day, all morning, how long, when, before, by the time, because
tip: Ask yourself: how long or how many? How long is about the activity, so use had been + -ing: I had been reading for an hour. How many is about the result, so use had + past participle: I had read fifty pages.

pick.q: We ___ for forty minutes when the waiter finally came.
pick.why: How long before a past moment ('when the waiter came'): had been waiting.

pick.q: His clothes were dirty because he ___ in the garden.
pick.why: His dirty clothes were a past result of an activity, so we use had been working.

pick.q: She ___ three cups of coffee by ten o'clock.
pick.why: 'Three cups' is a number, a finished result, so we use the past perfect simple: had drunk.

pick.q: I ___ him since high school, so I trusted him.
pick.why: Know is a state verb, so we don't use -ing: had known.

pick.q: How long ___ you been studying English before you came here?
pick.why: 'Before you came here' is a past moment, so we use How long had you been + -ing?

pick.q: The roads were flooded. It ___ for days.
pick.why: The flood was a past result of a long activity: had been raining.

pick.q: They had been ___ for an hour when the car broke down.
pick.why: After had been we use the -ing form: had been driving.

pick.q: My legs were sore because I ___ all afternoon.
pick.why: Had been + -ing for a long activity before a past result: had been standing.
